proof.text: Choose a coefficient subring of R. In equal characteristic its maximal ideal is zero and it is a field. In mixed characteristic its maximal ideal is generated by the nonzero p. Completeness implies separatedness; for a nonzero element the set of exponents for which it lies in (p)^n is bounded, so take its greatest member and divide by p^n to obtain a unit. Thus every nonzero element is a unit times a power of p. Every nonzero ideal is generated by an element of least such order, proving that the subring is a local PID with nonzero maximal ideal, hence a Cohen ring.

In the field case choose dim R parameters generating an ideal of definition I. In the Cohen case p is a nonzerodivisor. The dimension of R/pR is dim R minus one; choose a system of parameters in R/pR and lift it to R. Together with p the lifts generate I, with m^N contained in I and I contained in m.

R is I-adically complete by cofinality of the I-adic and m-adic filtrations. Evaluate power series over the coefficient ring at the lifted parameters using the complete power-series universal property. This ring map gives the required algebra structure. The maximal ideal of the source is generated by the variables (and p in the Cohen case), and its extension is I.

The source has dimension n in the field case and n+1 in the Cohen case. The number of parameters chosen above makes this equal to dim R. Since R is I-adically separated and powers of the source maximal ideal acting on R are I^k, R is Hausdorff as a module for that source ideal.

R/I is Artinian local. Its residue field is that of R, identified by the coefficient inclusion with the residue field of the source A. Hence its quotient by its Jacobson radical is cyclic as an A/m_A-module. The finite-length theorem for an Artinian local ring gives finiteness over A/m_A. The module R/(m_A R) identifies with R/I, yielding the last clause. In mixed characteristic p acts by zero on this quotient, so the argument is again over a field.

The coefficient-subring inclusion induces an isomorphism on residue fields. Every element of R/m_R therefore lifts from the coefficient subring. Evaluation fixes constants, so these lifts are also images of constant power series. This proves surjectivity of the composite A → R → R/m_R for the same parameter map chosen in the preceding steps.

title: Residue-preserving same-dimensional parameter map
statement: Let R be a commutative Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete local integral domain, complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. There exist a natural number n, a commutative coefficient ring Λ which is a field or a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], a local-ring structure on A = Λ[[X_1,...,X_n]] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and an A-algebra structure on R, such that dim A = dim R [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], the intersection of all submodules m_A^k R is zero, and R/(m_A R) [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] is a finitely generated A/m_A-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Moreover, the composite $A \to R \to R/\mathfrak m_R$ is surjective. No finiteness of R over A and no injectivity of A → R is assumed.

theorem complete_local_domain_residue_parameter_map
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (Λ : Type u) (_ : CommRing Λ),
      ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ))
        (_ : Algebra (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) R),
        (IsField Λ ∨ ∃ p : ℕ, IsCohenRing p Λ) ∧
        ringKrullDim (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) = ringKrullDim R ∧
        IsHausdorff (maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)) R ∧
        Module.Finite
          (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ ⧸ maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ))
          (R ⧸ (maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) • ⊤ :
            Submodule (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) R)) ∧
        Function.Surjective ((residue R).comp
          (algebraMap (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) R))
